avoid: flat full-screen UI with no device around it

rules.rule: Labels and cards go inward, into the negative space between the subjects (the empty wall, the floor), never pushed against the frame edges.
rules.why: the edges felt wasted and the labels read as stuck on

rules.rule: Callout dots, line ends and text never sit on a face: anchor on the torso or an object and lead the line away from the face.
rules.why: dots on faces looked like a mistake

rules.rule: A label sits beside or above what it names, never on top of it.
rules.why: the CRT label covered the screen it pointed at

rules.rule: When a label does not fit sideways, stack it into up to 3 short lines instead of forcing one long line out of the frame.
rules.why: tracked labels ran off the frame

rules.rule: No text on text and no card touching another card; title and subtitle keep a clear gap.
rules.why: 1985 and MARCUS overlapped; the two opening cards touched

rules.rule: A name stays close to its person: freeze titles hug the silhouette on both sides.
rules.why: Rex and Valance drifted to the frame edges

rules.rule: On a short shot a label must be readable from its first frame (no slow entrance) and hold long enough to read.
rules.why: the floppy label arrived too late to read

rules.rule: White text never sits on a white or busy plate: use a card (translucent pine with a thin cloud border) or move the text to a dark, calm area.
rules.why: white on white did not read

rules.rule: Titles and labels are sans (Inter Tight); the serif (Instrument Serif Italic) is only the accent line. Never let a font be substituted.
rules.why: a font fallback made every title serif and lifeless

rules.rule: Highlight key words with bold weight inside the line, not with more words.
rules.why: important words did not stand out

rules.rule: A spoken punchline lands word by word on the voice, big and bold (EVERY. / SINGLE. / TIME.), with a hit on each word.
rules.why: the line was too small and did not follow the voice

rules.rule: Nothing smaller than 36 px on screen.
rules.why: several texts could not be read

rules.rule: Logo: the mark lands first, then the wordmark slides out from behind it (Wordmark Reveal), on a musical downbeat.
rules.why: cross-family logo pattern from the Motion Style Map

rules.rule: Hits and punchlines use the Snap curve; fly-through transitions push into an object in the world (a screen) with Launch.
rules.why: editorial snap and push-through from the Motion Style Map

rules.rule: A heroic entrance gets a soft warm glow behind the person (backlight), not rays and not an outline around the silhouette.
rules.why: rays and contour lines read as too much

rules.rule: A UI on a screen sits inside the glass: clean the plate's screen, add the CRT bulge, blend it with the glass reflection, and keep the device in frame.
rules.why: a full-screen UI was not understood as a screen

rules.rule: Action lines are solid spark, short and punchy, when something great happens (raising the box).
rules.why: thin holographic lines did not read

rules.rule: Freeze titles: the person stays in colour (matte cut-out), the world goes black and white and defocused.
rules.why: the name frame needed the person to pop

rules.rule: Never cut a phrase: no cut inside a spoken word, and dialogue audio runs about 0.35 s past its cut.
rules.why: lines were chopped at the cut

rules.rule: Trim every AI shot to its action: no character appears where they never were, and plates end one frame before a camera cut.
rules.why: characters popped in at desks they never sat at

rules.rule: Music leads the key moments: it enters with the salesman, drops on his freeze, the bridge starts on a beat and the logo lands on a downbeat.
rules.why: music & edit findings of the Motion Style Map

rules.rule: Characters, location and props start as sheets; every shot is generated with those sheets as references.
rules.why: text-only shots drifted (faces, wardrobe)
